title: A Note on the Well Trajectory Tortuosity Index: Non-Independence of the Inclination–Azimuth Combination, and a Dimensionless Form
description: A note on the well-trajectory Tortuosity Index (TI) adapted to drilling by Ashok, Zhou, D'Angelo and co-workers (Zhou et al., SPE-178869-MS, 2016; D'Angelo et al., SPE/IADC-194099-MS, 2019) from the retinal-vessel measure of Grisan et al. (2008). It shows that the published inclination/azimuth root-sum-of-squares combination TI_3D = sqrt(TI_inc^2 + TI_azm^2) is not well-posed: the arc- and chord-length terms are the full three-dimensional quantities in both domain sums (only curve-turn detection differs), so the two components are not independent and any turn detected in both domains is double-counted, over-stating three-dimensional tortuosity by up to a factor of sqrt(2). The correction computes the index directly in three dimensions, sectionizing by curve-turn-plane-normal continuity (measuring each turn once and capturing torsion); a second correction removes the index's dependence on the unit of length, giving a dimensionless Modified Tortuosity Index (MTI). Both corrected forms are validated against a closed-form single-arc solution, dimensional and ordering invariants, and regression anchors on the ISCWSA standard wells, implemented as open-source tests in welleng. A naming collision is noted (the 'MTI' of SPE/IADC-194099-MS is an unrelated Mapped Tortuosity Index). The corrected 3D computation, the dimensionless form and the non-independence observation were described by the author in open-source form (welleng) and a 2022 blog series; this note consolidates and validates that material.
